# Bayer Aktie: Kurszielerhöhungen auf 66 Euro – Pharma überzeugt Analysten

Die Bayer Aktie erhält nach den Quartalszahlen weiteren Rückenwind von Analystenseite. UBS und Goldman Sachs haben ihre Kursziele für den Leverkusener Konzern auf jeweils 66 Euro angehoben, während die Deutsche Bank ihre Bewertung mit 60 Euro bestätigt. Alle drei Häuser empfehlen die Bayer Aktie zum Kauf. Ausschlaggebend sind vor allem die starke Entwicklung der Pharmasparte und deren weitere Wachstumsaussichten. Beim aktuellen XETRA-Kurs von 53,24 Euro ergibt sich aus dem durchschnittlichen Kursziel von 64 Euro ein rechnerisches Aufwärtspotenzial von 20,2 Prozent.

selected.thesis: Bayer reported strong quarterly figures on November 4, which triggered a significant re-rating from multiple tier-1 analysts including Goldman Sachs and UBS, both raising targets to 66 EUR. This reflects a disconnect between recent fundamental improvements and the current share price level. The convergence of positive earnings momentum and a concentrated cluster of price target increases creates a high-conviction window for a multi-day re-rating.
selected.why_move_is_not_spent: Despite the positive reaction on the earnings day, the current market price remains significantly below the new consensus targets (approx. 27% upside to the 66 EUR target). The magnitude of the analyst revisions following the 'strong numbers' suggests a sustained institutional rotation into the name that typically lasts beyond the initial 24-hour reaction.

# Deutsche Telekom lifts 2026 targets in Q3, buyback below forecasts

Published 05/11/2026, 06:48
...
Investing.com -- Deutsche Telekom nudged up its 2026 profit and cash flow targets on Thursday after T-Mobile U.S. drove a third-quarter earnings beat, but a planned 2027 share buyback of up to €2 billion came in below analyst expectations.

The company now expects 2026 adjusted core earnings (EBITDA AL) of around €47.6 billion, up from around €47.5 billion, and free cash flow AL of around €20.1 billion, up from around €20 billion, reflecting higher expectations at T-Mobile U.S. Analysts had forecast €47.06 billion and €19.74 billion.

selected.main_risk: Guidance was only confirmed, not raised, and semiconductor-equipment sentiment is poor after AI-infrastructure names were sold; a small-cap with a back-loaded year can also de-rate quickly if Q4 conversion slips.
selected.thesis: Nine-month order intake reached EUR 273.4m, up 55% year on year and a record for the period, far ahead of nine-month revenue of EUR 181.8m. With full-year revenue guidance only confirmed at EUR 255-275m, the order book mathematically forces a heavily back-loaded fourth quarter, and management explicitly points to a strong Q4 and clear growth into 2027 — a forward demand signal rather than a backward-looking profit beat.
selected.why_move_is_not_spent: The statement was published at 07:00 CET, ahead of the Xetra open, so the record order book has not been reflected in any cash-session price; the market's attention was on the reported revenue/EBITDA lines, which merely confirmed guidance, rather than on the order-intake lead indicator.

providers.market_view: German equities market shows elevated technical overbought conditions with multiple oscillators signaling potential pullback risk. Recent earnings season has driven significant moves in pharmaceutical and industrial names, but these catalysts are largely realized. Takeover situations show minimal arbitrage spreads with deals either fully priced or trading above offer levels. No clear forward catalysts identifiable within the 1-5 session horizon that haven't already been reflected in prices.

At the cutoff ahead of the Xetra open, German equities were in heavy Q3 reporting season with a mixed and selective backdrop. Several large caps had already reacted during the prior session, while a cluster of reports scheduled for later Nov 5-6 remained pending. With much company news already priced and morning releases lacking clear pre-open confirmation, remaining near-term long edge looked limited.
